Create a construction site organized around a tower crane and scaffolding, with stacked building materials, portable site cabins, fences, barriers, machinery, and debris. Let the crane provide the main vertical landmark while the scaffolding defines the active construction area below and around it. Group the building materials into recognizable stacks near the work area, keeping their placement deliberate rather than scattering every item evenly across the site. Position the portable cabins together beside an accessible part of the site so they read as a distinct support area. Use fences to define the site perimeter and barriers to separate material storage and machinery from the spaces between these groups. Place machinery near the active work and material-handling areas, with enough separation for each major piece to remain visible. Concentrate debris around the construction activity and beside stored materials, leaving some clearer gaps between the working area, cabin group, and storage stacks. Maintain a coherent construction-site layout in which the crane, scaffolding, cabins, materials, and machinery are all identifiable, with fences, barriers, and debris providing the smaller-scale context.
